question.text: Units of close-ended Alternative Investment Funds may be listed on stock exchanges with a minimum tradable lot of:

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM-Series-X-A (p.236) states that units of close-ended AIFs may be listed on a stock exchange with a minimum tradable lot of Rs. 1 crore, and listing is permitted only after the final close of the fund or scheme. The Trap: Listing alone does not change the AIF's investor-eligibility profile; the Rs. 1 crore minimum lot remains the binding threshold for secondary-market participation. Note: Broader claims about retail participation, market depth, ease of exit, or illiquidity until maturity are not in the checked page and should be cited from a separate source before being asserted.
